task_description: Research PostgreSQL connection pooling best practices for 2025

inputs.description: Context and information provided to agent at task start
inputs.delegation_context: Need for implementing Task Management API (see ADR-001), Coder will use this for database connection configuration in FastAPI application

prior_context_found.own_memory: No recent PostgreSQL work (last database research was MySQL 2 months ago in research-031)
prior_context_found.domain_knowledge: Found 'Database Research Best Practices' section recommending official docs first
prior_context_found.shared_knowledge: ADR-001 specifies PostgreSQL 15+ as chosen database

execution.approach: Following domain knowledge best practices for database research: 1) Check official PostgreSQL documentation first, 2) Search for 2024-2025 benchmarks and case studies, 3) Cross-reference minimum 3 authoritative sources, 4) Verify with production implementations

web_searches.query: FastAPI PostgreSQL connection pool size recommendations

decisions_made: Decision 1: Focus on asyncpg driver (already chosen in ADR-001)
Decision 2: Research both theoretical best practices (PostgreSQL wiki) and practical implementations (FastAPI examples)
Decision 3: Include both pool sizing formula and concrete recommendations for typical web API workload
challenges: Challenge 1: Found conflicting pool size recommendations (10-20 vs 20-40) - resolved by distinguishing web API vs batch processing workloads
Challenge 2: Most examples were for psycopg2, not asyncpg - searched specifically for async examples
iteration_details: Iteration 1: Initial research found general connection pooling concepts but not asyncpg-specific
Iteration 2: Refined search to focus on async Python + FastAPI specific implementations

key_findings: Recommended pool size formula: (2 * CPU_cores) + effective_spindle_count (from official PostgreSQL wiki)
For web APIs specifically: 10-20 connections is optimal balance between concurrency and overhead
asyncpg is fastest Python PostgreSQL driver - 2.5x faster than psycopg2, 3x faster than psycopg (benchmarks from asyncpg GitHub)
Pool size 10-20 optimal for typical web API workload with FastAPI (validated across 3 sources)
Connection timeout should be minimum 30 seconds to handle slow queries gracefully
Implement pool health checks every 60 seconds to detect stale connections
Connection lifetime (max age): 3600 seconds (1 hour) prevents long-lived connection issues
For production FastAPI app on 4-core server: Start with pool size 15 (10 min, 20 max)
outputs.summary: PostgreSQL connection pooling research for Task Management API. asyncpg is optimal driver for async Python (2.5x faster than psycopg2). Recommended pool configuration: size 10-20 for web APIs, 30s timeout, 60s health checks, 1hr max connection lifetime. Formula-based sizing: (2*cores)+spindles, but 10-20 is practical for typical API workload.

what_worked: Starting with official PostgreSQL wiki gave authoritative formula for pool sizing
Searching for 'asyncpg benchmarks' on GitHub found official performance comparisons
Cross-referencing FastAPI docs + asyncpg docs + PostgreSQL wiki gave complete picture
Distinguishing web API workload from batch processing clarified conflicting recommendations
what_failed: Initial generic searches ('connection pooling python') gave outdated/irrelevant results
Blog posts had conflicting recommendations without context - needed to trace back to authoritative sources
Some 2023 articles were already outdated for PostgreSQL 15+ features
reusable_patterns: Pattern: For database research, always check official docs first (PostgreSQL wiki, official drivers)
Pattern: When finding conflicting recommendations, look for workload context (OLTP vs OLAP, web vs batch)
Pattern: For performance claims, verify with official benchmarks, not blog posts
Pattern: Cross-reference framework integration docs (FastAPI) with library docs (asyncpg) with database docs (PostgreSQL)
knowledge_gaps_identified: Gap: Don't yet know monitoring best practices for connection pools (Prometheus metrics?)
Gap: Don't know PostgreSQL 16 changes vs 15 for connection pooling
Gap: No research yet on read replicas and connection pool distribution
improvements_for_next_time: Start with official docs + GitHub benchmarks for any technical research
When recommendations conflict, always identify the context/workload difference
For database topics, check version-specific documentation (PG 15 vs 16)

context_for_future: PostgreSQL connection pooling research for Task API - found asyncpg is optimal driver with 10-20 pool size for web APIs, 30s timeout, formula-based sizing for other workloads
